demos.title: Tutte’s squared rectangles
demos.summary: Turn a rectangle of unequal squares into a circuit. Inspect current balance, break the fit, and compare simple and compound constructions.

demos.title: Dijkstra shortest path
demos.summary: A generic weighted-graph solver with a certified shortest-path result.

demos.title: Flood fill + capability closure
demos.summary: Directed reachability across rooms, locks, keys, obstacles, and one-way ledges.

demos.title: Union-find percolation
demos.summary: A generic checked partition finds when open passages first cross a braided porous maze.

demos.title: Topological sort + cycle witness
demos.summary: A generic checked scheduler returns a complete legal order or an explicit directed dependency cycle.

demos.title: Aho–Corasick multi-pattern search
demos.summary: One checked byte automaton reports every exact match, including overlaps and duplicate patterns.

demos.title: LRU cache
demos.summary: A bounded key/value cache with proven recency, capacity, and least-recently-used eviction.

demos.title: A* heuristic search
demos.summary: A checked heuristic guides a generic shortest-path search. Compare its route and explored region with Dijkstra on weighted terrain.

demos.title: Tarjan strongly connected components
demos.summary: Find every group of mutually dependent modules, then collapse those groups into an acyclic graph.

demos.title: Token-bucket rate limiter
demos.summary: Watch a request burst spend available tokens, then refill over time. Exact integer arithmetic enforces the configured rate and burst capacity.

demos.title: Maximum flow / minimum cut
demos.summary: Change a connection's capacity and watch the bottleneck move. Lean returns a maximum flow and a minimum cut through a generic directed network.

demos.title: Myers shortest edit script
demos.summary: Edit two documents and inspect their smallest insertion/deletion script. Lean proves that replay reaches the target and no shorter script exists.

demos.title: Sweep-and-prune collision pairs
demos.summary: Drag moving boxes and see one-axis candidates narrowed to exact overlaps. Lean proves that no overlapping pair is missed or repeated.
